# Study 4 — sentence-only vs label-only injection: summary tables (generated by scripts/study4_analyze.py)

Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 2, α 5, their prompt and vectors; 20 fresh draws shared by all arms. Chance = 10%.

Sanity: S7 clean copies exact in 20/20 draws (D3 fix); example label part: “ SENTENCE 3:”, sentence part: “ A gardener trims the hedge.”.

## Arms (200 trials each)

| arm | push on | injected | clean reader | target copied exactly |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | sentence words | 97.5% (195/200; 95% CI 94.3–98.9) | 27.0% (54/200; 95% CI 21.3–33.5) | 150/200 |
| B | label "SENTENCE N:" | 64.0% (128/200; 95% CI 57.1–70.3) | 12.5% (25/200; 95% CI 8.6–17.8) | 191/200 |
| C | sentence words, random vector | 91.0% (182/200; 95% CI 86.2–94.2) | — | — |

**Main test (arm A, target copied exactly):** 150 trials; injected 145/150, reader 15/150 → **PASS** (needs ≥ 40 trials, injected ≥ 50%, reader ≤ 15%).

**Label test (arm B ≥ 100/200):** label highlighting IS a real alternative.

**Conclusion (pre-registered table):** **both routes work**. Secondary: arm-A loophole rule (all 200) → not confirmed; arm C vs A → within 10 points (not concept-specific).

Arm B copy-back: label copied correctly 200/200, sentence words intact 191/200.
